what_it_does: Quantum algorithms are valuable intellectual property, and when a company sends its circuit to an untrusted compiler service (a program that translates the algorithm into hardware instructions), that service could copy or reverse-engineer the design. TetrisLock addresses this by splitting the circuit into two interdependent pieces, like interlocking puzzle pieces: neither half reveals the full algorithm on its own, and only the legitimate owner who holds both halves can reconstruct the working circuit. The name alludes to Tetris-style interlocking shapes used to create this dependency. The scheme is designed so that even a malicious compiler cannot deduce the original algorithm from either piece alone.
